Comment 2: Additionally, inlaid and circular permutated base editors achieve similar functionality using a single transcript without increasing overall size.
Response: Thank you for the insightful comment. The inlaid and circular permutated base editors achieve similar functionality by embedding deaminases into nCas9(D10A) or permuting nCas9(D10A)’s domains 10. However, identifying the optimal embedding and permuting configurations for deaminases is time-consuming and labor-intensive. This is because that embedding deaminases (much larger than GCN4/gp41 epitopes) into nCas9(D10A) alters protein conformation and activity, limiting the number of viable embedding sites. Further, different deaminases have distinct optimal embedding sites due to variations in size and conformation. For example, mini-Sdd9’s inlaid and circular permutated base editors have 11 configurations, but only one performs well 11. Embedding TadA-TadA* into 43 positions of nCas9(D10A) results in only four variants with editing efficiency comparable to the original base editor 12. Additionally, the inlaid and circular permutated base editors possess relatively fixed editing windows, due to the limited configurations 10-12.
In contrast, embedding epitopes into nCas9(D10A) in the Plug-in BE system does not significantly alter the protein’s conformation (Figure 1B), therefore offer more flexibility. At VEGFA site 2, 50 out of 62 D10A-gp41 Plug-in CBE variants showed high C-to-T efficiency (Supplementary Figure 1B). Likewise, 24 out of 62 D10A-gp41 Plug-in ABE variants could achieve efficiently A-to-G conversion (Figure 3F). This flexibility of deaminase spatial localization endows Plug-in BE with more compatible editing window and capability of the Plug-in BE system for gene editing applications (Figure 6 and Supplementary Figure 11A).
Comment 3: Furthermore, this work lacks transcriptome and genomic-level off-target analysis data.
Response: Thank you for the helpful comment. According to your suggestion, we have conducted the off-target analysis for representative Plug-in ABE variants and Plug-in CBE variants.
1. Plug-in ABE Variants
1.1 DNA-level Off-target Analysis
To compare the off-target effects of MoonTag Plug-in ABE8eWQ (D10A-231gp41 and D10A-1020gp41) with ABE8eWQ, we conducted amplicon sequencing at the OCT4 site, HEK site 2, and their off-target sites 1-3 (Supplementary Figure 8A and B). D10A-231gp41 and D10A-1020gp41 demonstrated low off-target frequencies (<0.5%) at 15 sites in OCT4 and 19 sites in HEK site 2, comparable to ABE8eWQ. Notably, both variants reduced off-target effects at OT6 and OT7 in OCT4 (D10A-231gp41: p = 0.0332, p = 0.0172; D10A-1020gp41: p = 0.0341, p = 0.0173) and OT1 in HEK site 2 (D10A-231gp41: p = 0.0209; D10A-1020gp41: p = 0.0179). Overall, MoonTag Plug-in ABE8eWQ maintained high DNA-level specificity.
1.2 RNA-level Off-target Analysis
Adenine deaminase can deaminate adenine on the RNA chain into hypoxanthine, we therefore assessed RNA-level off-target effects of D10A-231gp41 and D10A-1020gp41 using mRNA sequencing (Supplementary Figure 8C and D). At the OCT4 site, D10A-231gp41 exhibited lower off-target effects than ABE8eWQ (p = 0.0272), while D10A-1020gp41 showed no significant difference. At HEK site 2, both D10A-231gp41 and D10A-1020gp41 had off-target effects comparable to ABE8eWQ. These transcriptome analyses confirm that MoonTag Plug-in ABE8eWQ does not increase RNA-level off-target effects.
2. Plug-in CBE Variants
To evaluate the DNA off-target effects of MoonTag Plug-in BE3 (D10A-1246gp41 and D10A-1252gp41), we conducted amplicon sequencing at HEK site 3, VEGFA site 2, and their off-target sites 4-6 (Supplementary Figure 8E and G). We calculated the on/off-target ratio to quantify the editing specificity (Supplementary Figure 8F and H). At VEGFA site 2, D10A-1246gp41 significantly improved the editing specificity at OT1 (p = 0.0436), OT4 (p = 0.0217), OT5 (p = 0.0207), and OT12 (p = 0.0080). D10A-1252gp41 enhanced the editing specificity at OT3 (p = 0.0077), OT4 (p = 0.0139), OT5 (p = 0.0019), OT6 (p = 0.0044), OT10 (p = 0.0252), and OT12 (p = 0.0153). At HEK site 3, both D10A-1246gp41 and D10A-1252gp41 exhibited similar specificity at four off-target sites. Overall, D10A-1246gp41 and D10A-1252gp41 showed comparable editing specificity to BE3.
